scope: Literature observations for screening only. Not training data, calibrated predictions, or proof of universal family performance.

sources.title: Oxidation of sulfamethoxazole and related antimicrobial agents by TiO2 photocatalysis
sources.review_note: Nanophase TiO2 was studied with aqueous SMX under UVA; catalyst identity and water constituents affected rates.

sources.title: Degradation of antibiotic sulfamethoxazole in aqueous media by UVA TiO2 pure brookite photocatalysis
sources.review_note: Phase pure brookite nanoparticles gave up to 88 percent SMX degradation after 180 minutes at pH 10 under UVA. Other conditions were investigated but are not all specified in the abstract.

sources.title: Removal of antibiotic sulfamethoxazole in water using rapid growing ZnO nanorod
sources.review_note: ZnO rods grown on kanthal wires were tested under UV. Reported SMX removal after 60 minutes differed with initial concentration; the 80 W and 120 minute values describe synthesis rather than treatment.

sources.title: Adsorption of sulfonamides from aqueous solution by carbon nanotubes determination of kinetics equilibrium and thermodynamic parameters
sources.review_note: CNT batch adsorption of SMX was reported with maximum uptake 207.0 mg per g at pH 3. A maximum capacity is not a removal percentage.

sources.title: Enhanced photocatalytic degradation of Amaranth dye on mesoporous anatase TiO2
sources.review_note: Urea assisted sol gel mesoporous anatase was studied under natural sunlight; its highest reported rate constant was 0.069 per minute. This is a specific synthesis and not generic P25.

sources.title: Degradation of Amaranth and Tropaeolin O in the presence of ZnO nanoparticles
sources.review_note: The abstract reports 74 percent amaranth degradation with light activated ZnO at 500 ppm. It does not specify the illumination wavelength or the associated contact time.

sources.title: Adsorption of Lead II Ions onto Magnetite Nanoparticles
sources.review_note: Commercial magnetite had about 10 nm mean particle diameter and BET area 115.3 m2 per g. Equilibrium conditions included pH 5, 25 C, 10 g per L and 240 minutes. Lead precipitation was observed above pH 5.4 in this setup.

sources.title: Removal of Pb II ions from aqueous solutions on few layered graphene oxide nanosheets
sources.review_note: Few layered GO prepared by a modified Hummers method adsorbed Pb II. Langmuir capacities of about 842, 1150 and 1850 mg per g were reported at 293, 313 and 333 K respectively; pH influenced adsorption.

sources.title: Heavy metal removal from aqueous systems using hydroxyapatite nanocrystals derived from clam shells
sources.location: Methods 2.5 to 2.9; results 3.1 to 3.4; Table 2; Table 5
sources.review_note: Clam shell derived hydroxyapatite rods were tested in batch and column experiments. Experimental batch maximum 265 mg per g differs from fitted Langmuir capacity 263.2 mg per g. These also differ from the column capacity 42.5 mg per g.

sources.title: Lead sorption from aqueous solutions on chitosan nanoparticles
sources.review_note: Chitosan tripolyphosphate particles of mean sizes 40 to 100 nm were prepared by ionic gelation. Langmuir lead capacity was 398 mg per g. Phosphoric groups and freeze drying influenced the material.

sources.title: Novel metal based nanocomposite for rapid and efficient removal of lead from contaminated wastewater sorption kinetics thermodynamics and mechanisms
sources.location: Results Adsorption isotherm studies; separate nMgO control sentence
sources.review_note: The paper mainly studies an MgO bentonite composite. It separately reports Langmuir capacity 55 mg per g for nMgO. Composite removal, recovery and regeneration findings must not be assigned to the standalone control.

sources.title: Shell biomass material supported nano-zero valent iron to remove Pb2+ and Cd2+ in water
sources.review_note: A shell-supported nZVI composite was tested for lead adsorption. The abstract reports 29.91 mg/g at pH 6; sample filtration is described in the methods. Do not transfer the composite result to unsupported iron.

sources.title: Adsorption characteristics of diclofenac and sulfamethoxazole to graphene oxide in aqueous solution
sources.review_note: Graphene oxide adsorbed up to 12 percent SMX within six hours. The exact time, dose, concentration and pH for this upper-bound result were not extracted; sonication produced a separate reported outcome.

sources.title: Assessment of sulfamethoxazole removal by nanoscale zerovalent iron
sources.review_note: At an nZVI-to-SMX mass ratio of 10:1 the abstract reports 83 to 91 percent removal in acidic conditions, without attributing the endpoints to individual pH values or times.

evidence.claim: Nanophase TiO2 under UVA degraded SMX; water composition and catalyst phase affected performance.
evidence.limitations: No exact operating point extracted. Does not define a universal pH range or a numerical removal prediction.

evidence.studied_pH_description: Reported study range endpoints only; intermediate tested values not extracted
evidence.claim: Brookite TiO2 gave up to 88 percent degradation at the stated pH and irradiation time.
evidence.limitations: Dose, initial concentration and irradiance not extracted. This optimum is not an applicability range.

evidence.claim: Wire supported ZnO nanorods removed the reported fraction of SMX under UV at 3 ppm initial concentration.
evidence.derivation: For dilute aqueous SMX, reported ppm concentration represented as mg/L; no conversion applied to catalyst ppm elsewhere.
evidence.limitations: Immobilized wire configuration; pH and light intensity not extracted. Synthesis power and duration are not reaction inputs.

evidence.claim: The same wire supported ZnO study reports this removal at 5 ppm initial SMX under UV.
evidence.derivation: Dilute aqueous pollutant ppm represented as mg/L.
evidence.limitations: Same study as E003; not independent replication and not comparable with a free ZnO powder by default.

evidence.claim: The same wire supported ZnO study reports this removal at 10 ppm initial SMX under UV.
evidence.derivation: Dilute aqueous pollutant ppm represented as mg/L.
evidence.limitations: Same study as E003 and E004. pH, catalyst mass and irradiance not extracted.

evidence.claim: CNTs have a reported maximum SMX uptake of 207 mg per g at pH 3.
evidence.limitations: Not removal efficiency; not a guarantee at another pH. Exact grade, dose, contact time and associated temperature not extracted.

evidence.claim: Urea assisted mesoporous anatase achieved the reported highest amaranth degradation rate constant under natural sunlight.
evidence.limitations: Do not convert to removal without a justified kinetic model. No pH, dose or concentration is attached from the abstract.

evidence.dose_reported: 500 ppm ZnO; mass basis not clarified in inspected abstract
evidence.claim: Light activated ZnO produced a reported maximum 74 percent amaranth degradation.
evidence.limitations: Do not infer wavelength, contact time or dose in g/L from this abstract. Unknown time prevents matching a requested treatment deadline.

evidence.concentration_reported: 0.5 to 5 mmol/L initial Pb II in equilibrium series
evidence.source_location: Abstract; section 2.3 equilibrium experiment; section 3.1 characterization
evidence.claim: A fitted maximum lead uptake was reported for the specified magnetite equilibrium experiment.
evidence.limitations: Capacity is not percent removal. Analytical filtration does not demonstrate magnetic recovery. Precipitation above pH 5.4 was reported only for this setup.

evidence.claim: Few layered GO had the reported fitted lead capacity at 293 K.
evidence.limitations: pH, dose and contact time for this capacity not extracted. An isotherm capacity cannot be compared directly with percent removal.

evidence.claim: The same GO study reported this fitted lead capacity at 313 K.
evidence.limitations: Temperature variant of E010, not an independent study. Other operating details remain unextracted.

evidence.claim: The same GO study reported this fitted lead capacity at 333 K.
evidence.limitations: Do not use this elevated temperature result as an ambient water prediction.

evidence.source_location: Methods Sorption capacity; Table 2 and results Sorption isotherms
evidence.derivation: 40 mg sorbent in 10 mL solution equals 4 g/L. Capacity series uses multiple initial concentrations, not one C0.
evidence.claim: Clam shell derived hydroxyapatite had measured maximum batch lead uptake of 265 mg per g.
evidence.limitations: Not the fitted Langmuir value of 263.2 mg/g. Do not transfer to column operation or an arbitrary hydroxyapatite product.

evidence.source_location: Methods contact time experiment; Results contact time and Figure 4
evidence.derivation: 40 mg in 10 mL equals 4 g/L; default pH 5 selected for subsequent experiments in the paper.
evidence.claim: Batch lead removal at the first 10 minute sample was reported as 99.0 plus or minus 1.0 percent.
evidence.limitations: Replicate uncertainty is reported by the paper, not an ML interval. High starting concentration and specific sorbent formulation limit transferability.

evidence.claim: The prepared chitosan tripolyphosphate nanoparticles had this fitted lead capacity.
evidence.limitations: Specific crosslinked and freeze dried formulation. pH, dose and time for the reported capacity not extracted. Cannot assign to unmodified bulk chitosan.

evidence.source_location: Results Adsorption isotherm studies; paragraph reporting nMgO control
evidence.claim: The full text separately reports a fitted maximum Pb II uptake of 55 mg per g for standalone nMgO.
evidence.limitations: Standalone control conditions are incompletely detailed. Do not borrow pH, regeneration, separation or real wastewater efficiencies from the MgO bentonite composite.

evidence.claim: The shell-supported nZVI composite had reported experimental lead adsorption capacity of 29.91 mg/g at pH 6.
evidence.limitations: Specific composite, not unsupported nZVI. Capacity is not percent removal. Other operating conditions are not attached to this abstract result; analytical filtration does not demonstrate complete material recovery.

evidence.claim: Study-specific graphene oxide adsorbed up to 12 percent SMX within six hours.
evidence.limitations: Upper bound over unspecified conditions, not a prediction or guaranteed removal. Exact time at maximum, pH, dose, concentration and temperature were not extracted. Sonication produced a separate reported outcome.

evidence.claim: At a 10:1 nZVI-to-SMX mass ratio, the abstract reports an 83–91 percent SMX removal range under acidic conditions.
evidence.limitations: Range endpoints are not attributed to exact pH values or time in the abstract. Do not treat it as a single experiment, guaranteed removal or a numerical prediction. Transformation products and recovery require separate consideration.

excluded_transfers.reported_claim: Composite capacity 75 mg/g and repeated use results
excluded_transfers.reason: Composite observations cannot be assigned to standalone MgO or nano clay. Bentonite used in this study was sieved at 53 micrometres; do not assume it meets the catalogue nanoclay dimensions.
These describe synthesis of the most promising sample. They are not photoreactor power and pollutant treatment time.

excluded_transfers.reported_claim: About 10 nm pore diameter in abstract
excluded_transfers.reason: Do not label a pore dimension as particle size. The 10 nm particle diameter used in profile P07 is separately supported by full text section 3.1.

excluded_transfers.formulation: CS HA batch and packed bed
excluded_transfers.reported_claim: 265 mg/g measured batch versus 263.2 mg/g fitted batch versus 42.5 mg/g column
excluded_transfers.reason: These are different outcomes and configurations. Only the measured batch value is attached to E013; no arbitrary conversion between them is allowed.
